call_points.text: FY27 revenue targeted at ₹14,000 Cr, while maintaining current margins.
FY27 capex planned at ₹2,050 Cr after ₹2,700 Cr invested over the last two years.
Management expects to maintain current EBITDA margins despite higher commodity prices, citing defence and international mix.
High ammonium nitrate prices could cause a demand contraction for a couple of months, but not for the full year.
Working capital days rose in Q4 due to higher inventory built against geopolitical risk; normalisation expected over the next two quarters.
Bhargavastra counter-drone product trials expected to be completed this calendar year.
Complete 155 mm round supply expected to start in 3 to 4 months after the coupling facility is finished.
FY27 revenue guided at ₹14,000 Cr against FY26's ₹9,838 Cr.
call_points.versus_prior: well above the ~15% medium-term CAGR guidance in memory

call_points.text: FY27 capex guided at ₹2,050 Cr, up from ₹1,556 Cr in FY26.
FY26 EBITDA margin was 27.95%, up 101 bps from 26.94% in FY25.
call_points.versus_prior: at the top of the 25-27% band in memory

call_points.text: Material consumed fell to 49.74% of sales in FY26 from 52.77% in FY25.
International sales rose 32% to ₹3,815 Cr, 39% of FY26 sales.
CIL sales fell 4% to ₹924 Cr in FY26, 9% of sales from 13%.

operating_notes.text: Order book was ₹21,200 Cr at 31 Dec 2025, of which ₹18,000 Cr was defence orders.
Defence contributed ~24% of 9MFY26 revenue versus 5% in FY21; exports were ~41% of 9MFY26 revenue.
Operating margin was 26.5% for 9MFY26, up from ~22.5% in FY21 and ~26% in FY25.
FY26 capex was ₹1,739.12 Cr against ₹1,005.95 Cr in FY25, with capital work-in-progress at ₹691.84 Cr at Mar-2026.
Ind AS 29 hyperinflation restatement on Turkey step-down subsidiaries cost ₹94.53 Cr in FY26 other expenses.
Outstanding NCDs were ₹11.67 Cr at 31 Mar 2026 after redemption of ₹15.00 Cr and ₹11.67 Cr tranches during the year.
FY26 order book ₹21,300 Cr across CIL & SCCL and Defence.
Defence sales ₹2,634 Cr in FY26, 27% of sales, up 94% YoY.
Net debt/EBITDA 0.32 and net debt/equity 0.13 at FY26.
FY26 order book ₹21,300 Cr: defence about ₹18,000 Cr (led by Pinaka) and non-defence about ₹3,000 Cr.
FY26 defence revenue ₹2,634 Cr, 27% of sales, up 94% YoY; Q4 defence revenue ₹1,008 Cr, up 134% YoY.
International sales crossed ₹3,800 Cr in FY26, up 32% YoY; management expects about 30% growth in FY27.
Secured export orders worth ₹1,076 Cr for Supply of Defence Products to be executed over 3 years.
Solar's Africa mining revenue is about $300 million and is expected to reach $900 million to $1 billion after combining with Omnia's BME business.
Omnia's BME explosives business currently earns EBITDA margins of 13-14% against a global explosives range of 18-19%.
Omnia recently added a 5,000-ton ammonium nitrate storage tank, doubling its storage capacity.

timeline.summary: 24 Apr 2026: CRISIL reaffirmed Solar Industries at AA+ and revised the outlook to Positive from Stable, withdrawing the rating on a fully redeemed ₹15 Cr NCD tranche.

Kailash Chandra Nuwal, Founder and Promoter of Solar Industries India Limited, declared no encumbrance on shares by him, his family (Mrs. Indira Kailashchandra Nuwal and Mr. Rahul Nuwal) or persons acting in concert, on 4th April 2026.
Sohan Devi Nand Lal Nuwal Family Trust declared no encumbrance on Solar Industries India Limited shares on 4 April 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,052.75 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹547.63 Cr.
15 May 2026: Q4FY26/FY26 investor presentation guides FY27 revenue to ₹14,000 Cr and capex to ₹2,050 Cr, with a ₹21,300 Cr order book and FY26 revenue up 30% to ₹9,838 Cr.
Solar Industries India Limited shared the earnings conference call recording link for Q4FY26 results on May 15, 2026, hosted by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited.
18 May 2026: Q4FY26 earnings call transcript reiterates FY27 revenue guidance of ₹14,000 Cr, defence target of ₹4,500 Cr and capex of ₹2,050 Cr.
Kailash Chandra Nuwal, Founder and Promoter, declared no encumbrance on Solar Industries India shares for KC Nuwal Group on April 4, 2026.
On May 29, 2026, Solar Industries secured an export defence order worth ₹1,076 Cr.

Solar Industries' step-down subsidiary signed definitive agreements to acquire South Africa's Omnia Holdings for $1.35 billion in cash, with management guiding combined FY28 revenue of ₹31,000-32,000 Cr.
Solar Industries' subsidiary Solar Explochem agreed to acquire Sivasakthi Industrial Explosives for ₹115.02 Cr on October 15, 2026.
